name: SPARE3D
ability_definition: The ability to imagine how something will look after it is moved around or when its parts are moved or rearranged.

task_realism.reasoning: Matching three-view orthographic drawings to an isometric view, and relating views to camera poses, are real skills used by drafters, mechanical engineers, machinists and inspectors when reading technical drawings. However, the objects are synthetic CAD primitives or ABC shapes rather than real assemblies, and the tasks never involve moving or rearranging parts, which is a core workplace use of this ability (assembly, maintenance, layout).

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: The test is a static, curated, clean line-drawing distribution with no ambiguity, noise, time pressure or stakes. Models are trained or fine-tuned on the same distribution, here with extra self-supervised CAD pretraining. Real work involves messy drawings, dimensions, annotations, partial information, and the option to use CAD tools or physical models. The i.i.d. benchmark setting overstates how well skill carries over to novel real objects.

construct_coverage.reasoning: It covers only one slice of the ability: mental rotation and viewpoint change of rigid single objects. Rearranging parts, imagining motion of mechanisms, folding or unfolding, and assembly or disassembly visualization are all absent. The three subtasks are also narrow and partly redundant, and the one generative task is rarely reported.

format_match.reasoning: The inputs, orthographic and isometric line drawings, resemble genuine engineering drawing artifacts, which is a strength. The outputs are forced four-way multiple choice rather than sketches, CAD models, or decisions about fit and interference, so the response format is artificial and permits elimination strategies.

transferability_reasoning: SPARE3D uses engineering-drawing-style inputs and tests orthographic-to-3D reasoning, which gives it some real relevance to drafting and engineering visualization. It is limited to multiple-choice, in-distribution evaluation of rigid-object viewpoint changes and omits part rearrangement and motion entirely. Transfer to broad workplace visualization is therefore modest.

2021.metric: accuracy (%) per task; no single aggregate metric

2023.model_or_system: Self-supervised spatial reasoning network (Xiang et al., CVPR 2022)
2023.metric: accuracy (%) on the SPARE3D 3-View to Isometric (T2I) 4-way multiple-choice task
2023.human_reference: General adult / relevant educated workforce (untrained adults performing everyday or technical spatial visualization, e.g., reading multi-view drawings)
